deferred.title: Literal domestic-product sales from final-sales statistic
deferred.reason: BEA Chapter2 footnote28 explicitly warns that inventories contain imported goods and source data do not separate imported inventory additions from direct sales. Final_sales=GDP-inventory_change is retained with this caveat, not advertised as a literal domestic sales observation; resolving that would need imported-inventory allocation data.

deferred.title: Saving from DPI as a new model
deferred.reason: S=DPI-personal_outlays is a qualified representation of b03 personal-saving-current-account after the source-defined DPI=PI-T substitution. Do not return it as separate new coverage. Personal saving rate, which defines a new dimensionless measurement, can be investigated separately with positive/zero denominator and signed-saving scope.

handoff.summary: Four independently defined national-accounting quantities: signed GDP-GDI statistical discrepancy, final sales of domestic product (with imported-inventory caveat), gross domestic purchases, and disposable personal income. All are current-price account flows/residuals, with signed adjustments retained. Earlier 23 model IDs preserved; no renamed algebraic inverses returned.
gaps: New account meanings and measured-boundary/time-vintage metadata required; monetary units alone do not enable safe runtime binding.
Final-sales interpretation limited by unknown imported inventory allocation.
BEA source/citation policies recorded; no comprehensive redistribution clearance inferred.
handoff.review_notes: Direct BEA glossary definitions, Chapter2 current framework/footnote28 and FAQ117/PIO additional definitions inspected 2026-11-01. Reviewed statistical-discrepancy sign and independent measurement, inventory volume valuation versus book stock, resident purchases versus domestic production, and personal-tax refunds versus social insurance/sales taxes. Independent synthetic error/origin/disposition ledgers test accounting identities, with zero or signed alternative cases. Actual JSON/ZIP validation logs accompany files; no scientific approval. Duplicate comparison includes own b01-b06 plus supplied inventory/runtime snapshot only. Toolkit JSON validation passed: four models, 12 arithmetic references and four rejection cases, all requires-extension; final edit revalidated before packing.

models.title: Signed statistical discrepancy between GDP and GDI
models.summary: Accounting residual between separately measured expenditure and income estimates of domestic production. Preserves the measurement discrepancy instead of imposing exact observed equality or interpreting it as a behavioral gap.

relationship.locator: Glossary definition and Chapter 2 printed 2-12/2-29 (PDF pp.12/29) product-to-income sign convention
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced SD labels the source discrepancy. Currency-currency=currency. Sign is expenditure estimate minus income estimate, confirmed by GDI=GDP-SD in handbook framework. Each amount represents the same period's production but different measurement approaches; no condition GDP=GDI imposed. Defining a residual is scientifically distinct from an extra expenditure component or a rearranged claim of equilibrium. No attribution of the discrepancy to either approach or a particular missing transaction is inferred.

variables.definition: Current-price expenditure-side estimate of domestic production.
variables.context: Same domestic economy, current accounting interval, current-price USD scale, data vintage and seasonal/annual-rate convention. GDP is the expenditure production estimate; GDI is independently measured domestic production income/costs, before any statistical discrepancy adjustment.
variables.domain: Finite estimate on the stated account/vintage basis.

variables.definition: Current-price income/cost-side estimate of the same domestic production, independently compiled.
variables.context: Same domestic economy, current accounting interval, current-price USD scale, data vintage and seasonal/annual-rate convention. GDP is the expenditure production estimate; GDI is independently measured domestic production income/costs, before any statistical discrepancy adjustment.
variables.domain: Finite estimate, with no assumption of observed equality to GDP.

variables.definition: Signed expenditure-minus-income residual for domestic production estimates.
variables.context: Same domestic economy, current accounting interval, current-price USD scale, data vintage and seasonal/annual-rate convention. GDP is the expenditure production estimate; GDI is independently measured domestic production income/costs, before any statistical discrepancy adjustment.
variables.domain: Finite signed; zero when estimates coincide, positive or negative otherwise.

assumptions: Source accounting convention: theoretical production coverage is common while source data/timing/measurement can differ.
Application scope: consistent current-dollar interval, annual-rate basis and data vintage; do not mix successive releases.
limitations: Residual does not identify which source is correct or estimate any particular error component.
Not excess demand, trade imbalance, a funding shortfall or a counterfactual equilibrium condition.

references.method: Independent constructed error decomposition around true synthetic production 1000: expenditure ledger duplicates 40 and income ledger omits 30. Known imposed measurement errors independently imply signed discrepancy 40+30=70. Counts of error entries supply expected residual; no claim actual BEA errors are known.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic two-measurement ledger; official source supports discrepancy concept, not these hypothetical errors.

references.method: Independent error construction: true synthetic production 970, expenditure coverage misses 20 while income ledger overcounts 30. Discrepancy from imposed errors is -20-30=-50, checking sign convention.
Identical estimates leave no measured residual; zero does not demonstrate absence of equal offsetting measurement errors.

rejection_cases.reason: Independent GDI estimate missing; cannot default to GDP or zero.

models.inverse_notes: GDP=GDI+SD given GDI,SD; GDI=GDP-SD given GDP,SD. Unique additive directions, no denominators or roots. Synthetic check SD=70,GDI=970 gives GDP=1040; forward SD=70. SD=0 gives equal estimates without singularity. Given only SD both levels are underdetermined. This scalar inversion does not correct source data or identify the true unobserved production value.

gaps: New GDI and statistical-discrepancy meanings; current-price GDP reused from b01 with matching vintage/context. Do not enforce a zero residual as an integration rule.

models.title: Current-price final sales of domestic product
models.summary: BEA-defined GDP excluding change in private inventories. Retains the source caveat that imported inventory changes prevent this statistic from strictly isolating actual sales of domestically produced output.

relationship.original_equation: Final sales of domestic product = GDP - change in private inventories.
relationship.locator: Glossary definition; Chapter 2 printed 2-14 (PDF p.14), especially footnote 28
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced FS,dInv name source prose quantities; GDP retained. Currency-currency=currency for flows over the same interval. dInv is a signed volume-change valuation, not closing inventory value minus opening book value. Source independently defines this aggregate despite its subtractive form; it is not a solve direction of b01 GDP, whose I input combines fixed and inventory investment. Do not strengthen the label into a literal domestic-sales classification: footnote 28 says inventory contains imports whose division between stocks and direct sales is not observed.

variables.definition: Current-price gross domestic product for the accounting interval.
variables.context: Same domestic NIPA accounting boundary, interval, current-price USD scale, vintage and annual-rate/seasonal convention. Inventory input is period-average-price volume change in privately owned inventories (including imported goods), not a book revaluation or inventory stock.
variables.domain: Finite accounting estimate, preserving source conventions.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced dInv = change in private inventories
variables.definition: Signed physical-volume change in privately owned inventories during the interval, valued at average prices of that interval under NIPA conventions.
variables.context: Same domestic NIPA accounting boundary, interval, current-price USD scale, vintage and annual-rate/seasonal convention. Inventory input is period-average-price volume change in privately owned inventories (including imported goods), not a book revaluation or inventory stock.
variables.domain: Finite signed; accumulation positive, liquidation negative; excludes pure inventory holding gains/losses.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced FS = final sales of domestic product
variables.definition: BEA aggregate GDP less private inventory change; does not strictly identify actual domestically produced goods sold.
variables.context: Same domestic NIPA accounting boundary, interval, current-price USD scale, vintage and annual-rate/seasonal convention. Inventory input is period-average-price volume change in privately owned inventories (including imported goods), not a book revaluation or inventory stock.
variables.domain: Finite signed accounting aggregate; retain definition and source caveat.

assumptions: Source definition: deduct complete NIPA change in private inventories from GDP.
Source limitation adopted explicitly: inventory additions include both domestic production and imports, and their allocation is unavailable in source data.
Application scope: additive current-price values, same interval/vintage and valuation conventions.
limitations: Not a literal observed total of domestic-output sales because imported inventories are not separately allocated.
Does not remove inventory price revaluation from raw company books; a correct NIPA volume-change input is required. No inventory forecasting.

references.method: Independent complete nominal expenditure ledger: PCE600, private fixed investment200, government100, net exports50, inventory additions50. Alternate source-defined final-use total excluding inventory is 600+200+100+50=950, while expenditure GDP includes the inventory flow and totals1000.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic disaggregated final-expenditure ledger, not published national data.

references.method: Independent alternate source sum: PCE700+private fixed investment200+government100+net exports(-30)=970. Here all 30 imports go into inventories; domestic final output sales total1000, GDP1000, private gross investment230, and inventory flow30. Thus statistic970 deliberately differs from literal domestic sales1000, testing source caveat rather than conflating them.
references.provenance: Curator complete hypothetical import/inventory ledger based on BEA footnote28; no source allocation data claimed.

references.method: Independent sales ledger with no imports: 1000 of current production plus 20 of prior domestic inventory sold to final users, giving 1020 final sales. Negative inventory investment correctly leaves final sales above current production.

rejection_cases.reason: Private inventory volume-change valuation missing; a stock value cannot be silently substituted.

models.inverse_notes: GDP=FS+dInv, dInv=GDP-FS, each unique when the other two quantities known, no denominator or roots. Ordinary ledger FS=950,dInv=50 recovers GDP=1000 and forward950. At dInv=0,FS=GDP without singularity; negative dInv is allowed. If only FS known, GDP and inventory change remain underdetermined. Algebraic recovery does not distinguish domestic versus imported inventories or identify actual domestic sales.

gaps: New final-sales and private-inventory-change meanings; current-price GDP reused. No binding from book inventory change or capital stock without a valuation adjustment model.

models.title: Current-price gross domestic purchases
models.summary: BEA final-purchase aggregate covering resident purchases regardless of production location. Distinguished from domestic production, with the sign of net exports retained.

relationship.original_equation: Gross domestic purchases = GDP - net exports of goods and services.
relationship.locator: Glossary definition; NIPA Chapter 2 printed 2-14 (PDF p.14)
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced DP labels source gross domestic purchases; NX=exports-imports. Currency-currency=currency. This independently named purchase aggregate differs from the geographic production boundary in GDP; negative NX raises DP relative to GDP arithmetically, without implying a causal import effect. It includes gross private domestic investment (fixed plus inventories), unlike final sales to domestic purchasers. Source alternate aggregation is C+I+G under full matching definitions, not a new equilibrium statement. No cross-border income adjustment as in GNP.

variables.definition: Current-price gross domestic product in the matching interval.
variables.context: Same domestic economy and resident-purchaser definition, accounting interval, current-price USD scale, vintage and seasonal/annual-rate conventions. GDP covers domestic production; NX is signed exports of goods/services minus imports, using matching NIPA classifications, not cross-border income.
variables.domain: Finite accounting estimate under source scope.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced NX = net exports of goods/services
variables.definition: Signed value of source-defined goods/services exports less imports for the same accounting interval.
variables.context: Same domestic economy and resident-purchaser definition, accounting interval, current-price USD scale, vintage and seasonal/annual-rate conventions. GDP covers domestic production; NX is signed exports of goods/services minus imports, using matching NIPA classifications, not cross-border income.
variables.domain: Finite signed; surplus positive, deficit negative; income transfers excluded.

variables.definition: Current-price resident final purchases under NIPA scope, including gross investment, regardless of production location.
variables.context: Same domestic economy and resident-purchaser definition, accounting interval, current-price USD scale, vintage and seasonal/annual-rate conventions. GDP covers domestic production; NX is signed exports of goods/services minus imports, using matching NIPA classifications, not cross-border income.
variables.domain: Finite accounting amount; not GDP or net national income.

assumptions: Source definition: GDP less net exports, equivalently PCE plus gross private domestic investment plus government consumption/gross investment.
Application scope: consistent nominal components, resident and geographic boundaries, interval and vintage.
limitations: Does not estimate imports, demand behavior or equilibrium; gross domestic purchases includes inventory investment.
No sum of independently chained-dollar components or automatic link to a different price index.

references.method: Independent origin/use ledger: domestic output1000, of which120 exported, leaves880 domestic output acquired by residents; imported resident final purchases200 make total resident purchases1080. Net exports120-200=-80. Alternate categories C700+I230+G150 also total1080, a cross-check rather than another GDP-NX evaluation.
references.provenance: Curator complete synthetic origin/final-use accounting ledger.

references.method: Independent resident-use ledger: domestic output1000, exports150, domestic output used by residents850 plus imports100, total resident purchases950. Net export surplus50; no income receipts/payments included.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic trade-surplus case, not observed economic data.

references.method: Equal export/import values leave gross domestic purchases numerically equal to GDP under the accounting definition; not a statement about how foreign trade changes actual production.

rejection_cases.reason: Net exports missing; cannot assume balanced trade.

models.inverse_notes: GDP=DP+NX and NX=GDP-DP, unique with other two values known; no denominator or branches. Deficit-ledger substitution DP=1080,NX=-80 recovers GDP=1000, forward1080. NX=0 yields DP=GDP without singularity. With only DP known, production and net exports remain underdetermined. No inverse identifies particular exports/imports: a net amount permits infinitely many directional pairs, and no causal response is asserted.

gaps: New net_exports_goods_services_current_price and gross_domestic_purchases_current_price meanings; GDP reused with compatible account context. Do not substitute GNP cross-border income or nominal account totals with chained-dollar values.

models.title: Disposable personal income after personal current taxes
models.summary: Current after-tax personal income available for outlays and saving under NIPA definitions. A distinct source-defined income aggregate, with net tax refunds and signed values preserved.

relationship.original_equation: Disposable personal income = personal income - personal current taxes.
relationship.locator: Glossary definition; FAQ117 opening paragraphs; PIO Additional Information definitions
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced PI,T,DPI label source prose quantities. Currency-currency=currency on a single current-price interval basis; DPI is a flow, not accumulated wealth. This newly named income definition is distinct from b03 personal saving, whose extra outlay input measures a different residual; do not submit the equivalent saving equation S=DPI-O as another new relationship. Source net-refund convention permits negative T. Do not subtract social-insurance contributions again from PI or sales taxes here. Matching SAAR levels produce SAAR DPI; they do not become literal one-month cash receipts without a separate time-basis conversion.

variables.definition: Source-defined current personal income accruing to persons before personal current taxes.
variables.context: Same NIPA persons sector, geography/residency boundary, current accounting interval, current-price USD scale, source vintage and adjustment/annual-rate convention. PI already follows NIPA treatment of social-insurance contributions; T is personal current taxes net of refunds, excluding sales taxes and other taxes classified outside this account.
variables.domain: Finite signed accounting amount on NIPA conventions; not just cash wages or capital gains.

variables.definition: Personal current tax payments net of refunds under source classification, for the same interval.
variables.context: Same NIPA persons sector, geography/residency boundary, current accounting interval, current-price USD scale, source vintage and adjustment/annual-rate convention. PI already follows NIPA treatment of social-insurance contributions; T is personal current taxes net of refunds, excluding sales taxes and other taxes classified outside this account.
variables.domain: Finite signed; a net refund can be negative; excludes sales taxes and social-insurance contributions in this subtraction.

variables.definition: Personal income after personal current taxes, available for personal outlays or saving.
variables.context: Same NIPA persons sector, geography/residency boundary, current accounting interval, current-price USD scale, source vintage and adjustment/annual-rate convention. PI already follows NIPA treatment of social-insurance contributions; T is personal current taxes net of refunds, excluding sales taxes and other taxes classified outside this account.
variables.domain: Finite signed current flow, with no invented nonnegative balance restriction.

assumptions: Source definition: subtract only personal current taxes from source-defined personal income.
Source convention: current taxes are net of refunds; PI already includes the source social-insurance adjustments.
Application scope: matching current-price account and time/annual-rate conventions.
limitations: Not take-home wages, bank deposits or change in wealth; NIPA personal income includes components beyond wages.
Does not evaluate tax laws or calculate tax liabilities; T is an observed/classified accounting input. No forecast or advice.

references.method: Independent uses-of-after-tax-income ledger: personal outlays780 and net current saving120 use900. Separate receipt ledger PI1000 includes source-compatible current income components and tax payment100. Expected DPI900 comes from the disposition side780+120, not another PI-T ordering.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic balanced current-income/disposition ledger; same constructed ordinary case as b03, new quantity rather than a new observation.

references.method: Independent disposition ledger after a net20 tax refund: outlays1000 plus saving20 use1020. Under source net-tax convention T=-20, and refund increases available current funds; social-insurance contributions are not subtracted twice.
references.provenance: Curator synthetic net-refund case supported by FAQ117 classification.

references.method: No personal current tax liability/refund means all source-defined PI is disposable; no inference that sales or payroll taxes vanish.

rejection_cases.reason: Personal current taxes missing; cannot silently substitute all tax payments or zero.

models.inverse_notes: PI=DPI+T or T=PI-DPI, unique with other two known; no denominator or root branches. Ordinary check DPI=900,T=100 gives PI=1000 and forward900. At T=0,DPI=PI nonsingular; with T=-20,PI=1000,DPI=1020, recovered refund is -20. If both PI,T unknown, DPI alone underdetermines them. Inversion never identifies legal tax obligations or the correct tax classification.

gaps: New disposable_personal_income_current_price meaning; PI and personal_current_taxes reuse b03 definitions. Context must preserve persons sector, net refunds, and SAAR versus literal period-flow basis.
